requirements.text: update their location to Lucknow Office at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM location WHERE location_id = 'LOC_024' AND name = 'Lucknow Office' AND city = 'Lucknow' AND state = 'Uttar Pradesh' AND country = 'India' AND active = 1
assumptions: no location named Lucknow Office, or in Lucknow, exists on the seed, so the request implies creating it (add_location is in the tools); implied by the request, not stated
id assumed next in sequence (LOC_024 after LOC_023); the only location the task creates
state written in full as the request gives it ('Uttar Pradesh') and as the benchmark check tests, although seed rows abbreviate states (LOC_004 has 'KA')
active = 1 kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
org_id, plot_no and street not stated and not tested

requirements.text: Kumar Mehta (kumar.mehta@company.com, +91-98101-00011, role Agent) has joined today
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE email = 'kumar.mehta@company.com' AND first_name = 'Kumar' AND last_name = 'Mehta' AND phone = '+91-98101-00011' AND role = 'agent' AND active = 1
requirements.source: Kumar Mehta's account is added at Lucknow office location
assumptions: two users are created in this table, so each is selected by its natural key (email), not by sequence position; neither email nor phone exists on the seed
role Agent maps to users.role = 'agent' (policy section 2 and the section 9 enumeration)
active = 1 because he 'has joined today'; the benchmark check agrees
phone tested as the request writes it, with hyphens; the seed stores phones in mixed formats, so if the tool normalises the format this cell will fail and should be relaxed
user_name, org_id and static_token not stated and not tested

disagreement: structure: A splits each benchmark user check into a create (identity, role, active, phone) and a change (location_id), B tests both in one create per user that also repeats the email in cells; kept A's split, one requirement per sentence of the request ('After creating both accounts, update their location' is its own sentence), so a run that creates a user but never locates them fails only the change; the benchmark check is carried jointly by both, and the predicates are the same conjunction

requirements.text: update their location to Lucknow Office at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM location WHERE location_id <> 'LOC_024' AND name = 'Lucknow Office'
assumptions: boundary of the location creation: one Lucknow Office, not one per user; the benchmark check counts exactly one row by name, which the id-anchored create alone would not enforce

disagreement: A writes this stay, B does not; kept because 'update their location' names one office for two users and a second row would fail the benchmark's count while passing the create; cells written with the row key in the selector and the tested name as the cell (A's sql with the terms reordered)

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on all three benchmark checks (kept), the new location (LOC_024: Lucknow Office, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, active), the two users selected by email (Kumar Mehta agent and active, Arpit Singh manager and inactive, phones as written) and their location_id = LOC_024.
disagreement: structure of the user checks: A a create plus a change per user, B one create per user carrying location_id and repeating the email in cells; kept A's split, one requirement per sentence of the request, with the benchmark check carried jointly (logged in each create).
disagreement: a stay that no second Lucknow Office row exists: A writes it, B does not; kept as the boundary of the create, since the benchmark counts exactly one row by name (logged in the requirement).
disagreement: a stay that LOC_004 (Bangalore Support Center, the seed's only India location) keeps its name, city and country: A writes it, B does not; dropped because no listed tool writes an existing location row (the tools are add_location, find_locations, add_new_user, update_user_details, get_user), and the misuse it would catch (locating the users at LOC_004 instead of a new office) already fails the location_id = LOC_024 cells; a stay nothing can break makes the file longer without making it stricter.
Seed facts re-checked at merge: no user has either email or phone; no location is named Lucknow Office or sits in Lucknow (the three '...Office' rows are NYC Sales Office, Initech Office Park, Vehement Offices); LOC_004 is the only India location (state 'KA'); LOC_023 and USER_100 are the highest ids; the acting user USER_039 is an admin (full CRUD), so the policy allows every step. A policy tension is left to the agent: section 8.1 says an updated user must be active, yet Arpit's account is given a location while inactive; the benchmark expects the update to happen and only the final state is tested.
